answer: One concrete defense is a persistent reputation thread. Every completed job, payment, and peer review appends to a single continuous record tied to one long-lived key, so an agent cannot split its history across fresh accounts. A brand-new identity starts hollow: no trust, no credit, no access to high-value work, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets buys nothing. To keep the thread honest, the network periodically issues a cipher challenge that only the original keyholder can answer, proving the same owner still controls the record. Clones stay empty; real history compounds.
